claim: The NixOS manual's canonical out-of-tree test invocation is 'let pkgs = import <nixpkgs> {}; in pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest { imports = [ ./test.nix ]; defaults.services.foo.package = mypkg; }' — an imports-based test module plus a defaults block injecting the caller's own package into all nodes.
stance_target: A project flake with its own nixpkgs input defines its own NixOS test via runNixOSTest with imports + defaults, not by copying in-tree nixosTests wiring
scope_conditions: NixOS manual stable, sec-calling-test, 'Testing outside the NixOS project'
quoted_support: Outside the nixpkgs repository, you can use the runNixOSTest function from pkgs.testers: let pkgs = import <nixpkgs> { }; in pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest { imports = [ ./test.nix ]; defaults.services.foo.package = mypkg; } runNixOSTest returns a derivation that runs the test.

claim: runNixOSTest accepts the test as a module (imports = [ ./test.nix ]) where the test module carries nodes.<name> (QEMU VMs as NixOS modules) and testScript (Python code); machines are implicitly started on the first action and start_all() starts all in parallel.
stance_target: The test gate's test.nix carries nodes.mqtt.server + nodes.mqtt.agent and a Python testScript
scope_conditions: NixOS manual stable, test framework chapters
quoted_support: We refer to the whole test above as a test module, whereas the values in nodes.<name> and containers.<name> are NixOS modules themselves. The option testScript is a piece of Python code that executes the test ... The first line is technically unnecessary; machines are implicitly started when you first execute an action on them (such as wait_for_unit or succeed). If you have multiple machines, you can speed up the test by starting them in parallel: start_all()

claim: The defaults attribute applies NixOS options to all machines in the test (both QEMU VMs and systemd-nspawn containers); nodeDefaults/containerDefaults give per-type defaults.
stance_target: A flake can inject its own agent package into every test node with one defaults block
quoted_support: To set NixOS options for all machines in the test, use the attribute defaults. These options are applied to both virtual machines and containers. You can set separate defaults for virtual machines and containers using the attributes nodeDefaults and containerDefaults, respectively.

claim: The test script has copy_from_host(source, target) to copy a file from the build sandbox host into the guest VM (via the shared_dir directory), and copy_from_host_via_shell as a fallback without a shared folder.
stance_target: Config files or the built agent binary can be shipped into the test VM without extra wiring
scope_conditions: NixOS manual stable, machine object methods
quoted_support: copy_from_host(source, target) Copies a file from host to machine, e.g., copy_from_host("myfile", "/etc/my/important/file"). ... The file is copied via the shared_dir directory which is shared among all the machines (using a temporary directory).

claim: Normal runNixOSTest builds run headless (the derivation just runs the QEMU VMs and the Python driver); interactivity is opt-in through the test derivation's .driverInteractive attribute, and the interactive submodule merges extra config (e.g. interactive.nodes.rabbitmq) only when running interactively.
stance_target: A CI test gate needs no display and no special config to run in QEMU headlessly; driverInteractive is the debugging escape hatch
scope_conditions: NixOS manual stable, interactive option + driverInteractive
quoted_support: Tests can be run interactively using the program in the test derivation's .driverInteractive attribute. When they are, the configuration will include anything set in this submodule. You can set any top-level test option here. Example test module: ... interactive.nodes.rabbitmq = { services.rabbitmq.managementPlugin.enable = true; };

claim: QEMU VMs vs systemd-nspawn containers are both available as machine types; VMs are needed for kernel features, X11, systemd namespacing options and setuid, while containers are faster and lighter for CI.
stance_target: Whether the test gate should use a VM or a container for the broker + agent topology
quoted_support: Containers share the kernel of the host system; they are significantly faster to start up than virtual machines. ... Virtual machines allow testing NixOS modules that use systemd's namespacing options (such as ProtectSystem= or MountAPIVFS=).
